text:
maria: Heads up — p95 for /v1/generate in eu-west is showing ~120ms but p50 is ~200ms. Looks inverted, spotted on the dashboard this morning. Anyone else?

sam: Huh, that sounds impossible unless we're mixing sample sets. Got a screenshot or query link? :thinking_face:

maria: https://console/redwood/dashboards/xyz — zoomed to last 6h. I pulled raw numbers from metrics API: p50=200, p95=120 for endpoint=/v1/generate region=eu-west route=primary

devon: Possible sampling or rollup bug. Did we change rollout sampling rules last night for fallback routing? @maria when did the new routing policy land?

maria: Rollout went live ~00:30 UTC. We introduced fallback route with weight=0.2 for small-customers to reduce cold-starts.

luis: Quick hypothesis: fallback traffic has lots of tiny latency samples (micro-batched or cached), and our rollup merged primary+fallback sketches incorrectly — sample_origin tags might've been dropped during aggregation.

ashley: If fallback has lower tail and many samples, merging sketches can drag p95 down. But p95 < p50 suggests the percentiles are being computed across different sample populations (e.g., p50 from full population, p95 from subset).

sam: Can you share the query you used to pull raw numbers? I'll try to reproduce against raw telemetry store.

maria: Sure, ran this against metrics-api: ```
SELECT
  approx_quantiles(latency_ms, 100) AS qtiles,
  count(*) AS cnt
FROM telemetry
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND region = 'eu-west' AND ts > now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY sample_origin
```

maria: Results: sample_origin=primary -> p50=220 p95=300; sample_origin=fallback -> p50=40 p95=70; console rollup (endpoint+region) shows p50=200 p95=120 (weird).

devon: That nails it. Console rollup is using merged t-digests but with inconsistent weighting logic when merging subgroups. If it used sample counts from inconsistent windows or overwrote origin tags, the merged digest can be nonsensical.

luis: Details: our rollup path does incremental merges: sketches from edge -> aggregator -> longterm store. Edge adds sample_origin tag but aggregator currently strips it for ``endpoint`` aggregation to save cardinality. Stripping means the aggregator merges fallback+primary as a single digest but still keeps the per-origin quantiles somewhere else; then when UI fetches p50/p95 it may be mixing pre-merge and post-merge values due to cache hit timings.

ashley: Two-pronged fix: 1) short-term: make dashboard SLO views exclude sample_origin=fallback by default (or add a toggle). 2) long-term: preserve sample_origin in rollup keys or keep per-origin sketches and do a proper weighted merge that respects counts and timestamps.
sam: Agreed. For short-term, can we hotfix the dashboard query to filter out fallback for SLO charts? That should restore sane p95 for alerts.
maria: I can file a PR to change the SLO dashboard backend to add "exclude: sample_origin=fallback" and surface a toggle 'include fallbacks' in the console.
devon: Also audit the merge implementation — our t-digest merge currently multiplies centroids by sample_count but we forgot to normalize when centroids came from already-merged sketches. Edge cases with mixed sketch compression can invert quantiles. I'll open an infra ticket to fix merge semantics.
luis: Meanwhile, small telemetry improvement: start propagating x-route-weight and x-sample-origin headers from the gateway through the proxy so the aggregator doesn't have to infer origin. That'll reduce ambiguity.
maria: I'll add x-route-weight header and ensure istio route rule forwards it. Will also add a short migration plan in console release notes.
sam: deploy-bot: rolling canary deployed last night for fallback routing at 00:30 UTC. Any rollback needed?
deploy-bot: Canary active -> traffic fraction 20% -> no automated rollback triggered.

maria: No rollback yet — this is more a visibility/aggregation correctness issue than user-impacting latency. But I'll prioritize the dashboard hotfix + telemetry header change. Filing tasks now.

ashley: UX ask: add small helper text on pctl chart explaining "percentiles reflect the merged rollup across origins; use toggle to isolate origins" — reduces confusion for oncall.

maria: Good call. Adding to PR. I'll post the ticket numbers when created. :+1:
